description: Known suspicious packaging patterns that may indicate counterfeit or substandard medicines. These patterns are based on common counterfeiting indicators identified in pharmacology literature.

patterns.explanation: The packaging makes extraordinary cure claims that are not typical of legitimate pharmaceutical products. Legitimate medicines do not claim to cure multiple serious diseases.
The packaging uses exaggerated efficacy language uncommon in legitimate pharmaceutical labeling, which must comply with regulatory standards.
The packaging claims no side effects. All legitimate medicines are required to list potential side effects. This claim is a common indicator of counterfeit products.
The packaging makes regulatory approval claims combined with origin indicators that may not align. Verify FDA approval status directly at fda.gov.
The packaging references secret or proprietary formulas without listing specific active ingredients. Legitimate medicines must disclose their active ingredients.
The active ingredients are listed as unknown or proprietary. Legitimate pharmaceutical products must clearly state their active ingredients and strengths.
The packaging uses marketing urgency language uncommon in legitimate pharmaceutical labeling. Medicine packaging typically does not use sales-style language.
